answer: Because the harbor audit recomputes usage from the nebula history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 180 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 79 keys therefore forfeits for 79 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the marble declaration. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
